utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. First of all, for the record, I indicate that we convene -- reconvene under Rule 15 bis, Judge Harhoff being absent. Good afternoon to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm Tom Hannis, along with Matthew Olmsted, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, Ms. Dierdre Montgomery, and Danko Kostovic, appearing for Stanisic Defence this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Igor Pantelic, and Aleksandar Aleksic for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber has one housekeeping matter before we continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yesterday the Office of the Prosecution filed a motion to amend its 65 ter list to reinstate a document, and the -- it would be useful if the Defence would indicate if -- if they could indicate orally whether they have an objection. If not, we would request your response by day after tomorrow, Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Your Honours, that we are not in a position to state our position at this moment. But if Your Honours will indulge us, during the course of the day we would be able to give you our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I suppose Mr. Krgovic says the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Are there any other matters that we need ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PLAVEC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as the counsel for the witness, I would like to ask something of the Chamber. Yesterday the witness felt a strong stab of pain in his cervical vertebra and he thinks this was because he was sitting for an extended period of time. He believes that he will not be able to sit for five hours, and he believes that he would be able to take four hours of sitting down, and we would therefore kindly ask the sitting hours to be curtailed by one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. We have been alerted to that request being made, and we agree. We are going to work out the exact time that we would rise, but you may assure your client that we will -- that today's schedule will accommodate him in that regard. So it -- we will see how the -- what progress we make, and the question is whether we would sit for a portion of what would ordinarily have been the third session, or whether it would be -- the practical course would be to vacate that session entirely. But we will see how we go in that regard. Thank you. You have something to add to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just related to that, Your Honour, I would indicate that the next witness to follow, ST-217, is only arriving tonight. I think Ms. Korner sent an e-mail to Ms. Featherstone advising of that, and therefore will only be seen for proofing in the morning and wouldn't be ready to start in the morning in the off chance that we were finished with this witness by then. So we propose that ST-217 not begin his testimony until Friday morning. If we're done earlier tomorrow, that would be a time we would propose to discuss exhumations and Mladic materials and any other housekeeping matters that are appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we are all on notice in that regard. Yes, and now those matters having been settled, we would now return to closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As I said, Your Honours, we were invited to give our position on the -- on the motion to amend the 65 ter list, and Mr. Pantelic will address that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, first of all, I would kindly ask, in future, that our friends from the Prosecution office mark these kind of motions with numbers. It will be easier for us to follow and to have a systematic view. This particular motion is 52nd or 53rd motion, and given the fact that this trial started last September, the average filing of these sort of motions is one per week. And this is a clear illustration how our friends from the Prosecution actually are not able to present its case and they are not familiar with -- with its own case, Your Honours. This is a -- this is a serious violation of the rights of the accused, this way, this practice. Because with regard to my client, Mr. Zupljanin, they filed indictment in 1999, 11 years ago, and, finally, this trial started in September last year, where everyone could, I said, accept that Office of the Prosecution is ready for trial and know what its case is. And this unacceptable practice must stop, Your Honour. That's why we strongly object to -- with regard to the admission of this particular document. And in addition to that, Your Honour, I don't know who the author of this particular motion was, but maybe he or she was not informed. I'm referring to the page 2 of this motion. There is some explanation that in relation to previous Exhibit P668, this particular document will give the Chamber a greater insight into the accused Zupljanin's authority in relation to local war president. This is completely ungrounded and completely misunderstanding of this particular motion, and in addition to that, these kinds of submissions should be addressed for the final submission not to use it during the course of the trial. So for all these reasons, Your Honours, I am completely -- I strongly object to this -- to this -- to admission of this document, because it is a clear example of the lack of diligence on the part of the OTP. We have Rules here, we have a framework of our activities here, and this is really not along the lines with these standards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the sermonette that you just treated us to indicates your -- your position on this, or do you intend to file a written response?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, I'm absolutely comfortable with the oral response and we are objecting to the admission of this document on this basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So noted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All can I say to that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We weren't inviting a response, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No you weren't, but I'm applying, I suppose, as they're not putting in a written response to which we would have a right to ask for a response to the response. I simply want to say this, Your Honour, in one sentence: In Mr. Pantelic's sermon, as I think Your Honour called it, although that's come out as something different in the LiveNote, he actually failed to point to any prejudice that the Defence can suffer from this. They have had this document for months, we've explained how it's come about, that it was removed, and we say its probative value far outweighs any prejudice. But Your Honours, actually what I wanted to deal with, I'm afraid, are a number of really rather urgent administrative matters, particularly in light of Your Honours' and indeed Your Honours' staff absence next week. Your Honours, can I just say straight away, strangely enough, after a year of trial, the anniversary being yesterday, we are reaching the end of the Prosecution case. Our estimate with the present new witnesses is that we will finish the Prosecution case mid-November, roughly about seven weeks. Your Honour, there are still -- and I'm sorry, I know this is the drum I keep beating, but a large number of important outstanding decisions for Your Honours to make on motions from both sides. The first is this, and that is you haven't yet ruled as to whether Ewan Brown may be treated as an expert. We filed an application way back last year for a number of people, and Your Honours' rulings have come effectively just before the witness testifies. Mr. Brown, there are difficulties with him. He no longer works at the Office of the Prosecutor. He is self-employed, and he has undertaken a long contract which is going to last three months which starts next week. Now, he has very kindly agreed, as we understand it - we're still awaiting the final confirmation because it's a contract that will take him out of Europe - that he can testify the week of the 18th of October, which is not that far away. So we need to know whether he will be treated as an expert because it depends on whether his report goes in and all of that. Second matter is this, which is linked: We applied -- Your Honours said that we could only apply to add the Mladic notebooks to our 65 ter list and not have them exhibited, or we said that's what we were planning to do. We actually applied to do that on a 18th of May. You came back to us on the 29th of June and said only specific entries as opposed to all the notebooks, which we supplied on the 13th of July, the excerpts that we wish to have entered as exhibits. And we have not had a ruling on that and we do really need a ruling. It affects, or may affect, Mr. Brown's evidence. In addition to that, Your Honours, we asked whether the Defence were still maintaining their challenge to the authenticity. They said they were, in which case we said we needed to add to our list two witnesses who dealt with the authenticity. So that needs to be dealt with. Your Honour, we are disclosing -- we're going to, in fact, today give the Defence a spreadsheet which contains a summary of what is on all the tapes, the audio and videotapes, which is being done by the OTP. Mr. Zecevic raised this in the absence of both Mr. Hannis and myself, I think, on the 2nd of September, and said that he was going to be applying for an adjournment. We have decided, because we part-disclosed the tapes already, the remaining tapes we will disclose but we are saying that none of them -- not none of them, I think maybe three or four could be said to have any relevance to this case at all. They deal, in the main, with what seems to have happened either in Croatia in 1991 or well beyond the scope of this indictment. And to assist the Defence, we've given them the spreadsheet. And so obviously we would be saying we object to any adjournment, that -- for the basis of examining these tapes because we say they are utterly and wholly irrelevant as will be seen from our summary of what's on the tapes. Your Honour, the other matter is there are -- we put in an application to call two further witnesses on the 8th of July to deal not with adjudicated facts that Your Honours had struck out or in some way altered but to deal specifically with Defence challenges. And the Defence responded to that, and we put in a response to the response on the 27th of July. Again, for purposes of timing, we do need to have a ruling on those two witnesses who are named there ST-041 and ST-055. As I say, they are specifically to deal with Defence challenges to adjudicated facts. And those, Your Honours are the administrative matters which I wish to draw to your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. The only thing I would say now is that the last item you mentioned, you could expect that ruling imminently.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, but as I say, all the ones that I have mentioned, not to mention the other ones --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, we haven't lost sight of that. It's just that because of our familiarity, recent familiarity with that, I -- I -- I can assure you that that one is -- you could expect very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Which doesn't mean, Ms. Korner, that the other ones you cannot expect very soon, it's just that we remember this one very well for the moment, but there are other ones to come as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I believe we are in Courtroom I tomorrow. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of September, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.45 p.m.,
